deaths occur in vehicles.

crossings which are potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not
attempt to cross flooded roads. Find an alternate route.

Arroyos, streams, and normally dry rivers can become raging killer
currents in a matter of minutes. Water in arroyos can travel many
miles and take hours to reach your location from upstream rain areas.

Health Advisory effective for Shelby County Tennessee, Crittenden
County Arkansas, and DeSoto County Mississippi, including the city
of Memphis that will remain in effect until sunset. This ozone health
advisory is due to monitored ozone values that are unhealthy for
sensitive groups. These values have exceeded the Environmental
Protection Agency's federal safe health standard. The Shelby County
Health Department recommends that sensitive groups which include
active children and adults, and people with respiratory disease,
such as asthma, limit prolonged outdoor exertion.

Forecast effective for Shelby County Tennessee, Crittenden County
Arkansas, and DeSoto County Mississippi, including the city of
Memphis for Saturday. This ozone forecast is due to forecasted ozone
values that will be unhealthy for sensitive groups. These values will
exceed the Environmental Protection Agency's federal safe health
standard. The Shelby County Health Department recommends that
sensitive groups which include active children and adults, and
people with respiratory disease, such as asthma, limit prolonged
outdoor exertion.

Please continue to check the latest air quality forecasts and updates
until monitored values return to safe levels. For more information go
to www.airnow.gov.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 18 at 2:50PM MDT until September 18 at 5:45PM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Northeastern Davis County in northern Utah...
South Central Weber County in northern Utah...

* WHEN...Until 545 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas due
to heavy rainfall from strong thunderstorms. River or stream flows,
especially along the Weber River, are expected to rise.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 248 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Public reported minor flooding is already
occurring in the advisory area. Between 0.75 and 1.25 inches of
rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 18 at 11:29AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
Heavy rain and strong winds are expected to start later today and
last
through the weekend as multiple strong low pressure systems move
into the northern gulf. These lows will bring multiple days of
moderate to heavy rain, with around 1.5 to 3 inches of rain every 24
hours. Some areas, especially near Yakutat and along the gulf coast,
could see localized areas reach around 4 inches of rain in 24 hours.
Heaviest rain rates are anticipated late Saturday into Sunday with
hourly rates of 0.15 to 0.3 inches possible. This heavy rain will
likely cause rapid river rises along smaller rivers and streams, but
no flooding is expected at this time.

Along with this heavy rain, increased winds are highly likely across
the area. Strongest winds are anticipated to occur late Saturday
into Sunday with 30 to 40 kts, gusts to 50 kts across the gulf and
20 to 35 kts, gusts around 40 to 50 kts across the northern inner
channels. Land winds will also increase, with areas especially along
the gulf coast seeing wind gusts up to around 45 mph. Check back for
more updates through the weekend.

properties.headline: Hydrologic Outlook issued September 18 at 10:20AM MDT by NWS Riverton WY
properties.description:
ESFRIW

A wet weather system will support periods of showers and
thunderstorms across Wyoming Friday, Saturday, and Sunday. This
weather system is funneling abundant tropical moisture into the
state. Given this anomalously high moisture, many thunderstorms will
feature heavy rainfall, possibly leading to localized flooding. Poor
drainage areas, urban areas, and steep terrain will be the most
susceptible locations for this isolated flooding.

Many locations could see rainfall totals anywhere between 0.75" to
1.75" through Sunday afternoon, with a majority of this rain falling
quickly in thunderstorms.

Remember, if you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around don't down!

properties.description:
ESFAFG

...Locations Impacted...
Upper Kuskokwim Valley

River levels on the Kuskokwim River at McGrath may still rise this
afternoon in response to the heavy rain earlier this week. The
Kuskokwim has leveled out around 18.5ft as of 6 AM AKDT Friday
morning, there is a chance for it to rise back up to near bankfull
later today or tonight. If the river looks to drop, this will be the
last update.

properties.areaDesc: Citrus, FL; Levy, FL; Marion, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 18 at 9:18AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus
Counties.

.The Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon has been steadily rising since
July, and on September 15 reached flood stage. The cause of the high
water along the Withlacoochee River at Dunnellon is due to excessive
hydrilla growth (from the river bottom to the water surface) along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between US 41 and Lake Rousseau.  The
hydrilla is acting like a dam and holding water back, causing water
levels to rise.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 AM EDT Friday the stage was 28.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage this
afternoon and continue rising to 28.2 feet this afternoon.
Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.2
feet on 10/02/1979.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued late tonight at 1215 AM EDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued September 18 at 8:15AM CDT until September 19 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Little Rock AR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heat index values up to 106.

* WHERE...Prairie, White, Jackson, Lawrence, Monroe, Randolph,
Woodruff, Independence, Sharp, and Arkansas Counties.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Hot temperatures and high humidity may cause heat
illnesses.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

properties.areaDesc: Upper Chena River Valley; Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 18 at 4:31AM AKDT until September 19 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Including the following areas, Fairbanks, North Pole, Two
Rivers, Fort Wainwright, Ester, and Fox

* WHEN...Through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rain may result in minor flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- The Chena River is running higher than normal and will continue
to be high through the week. As of 4 AM AKDT Friday, river levels
near the Upper Chena have crested and are beginning to come down.
The Chena below Hunts Creek is still rising gradually but
beginning to level off. The Chena below Moose Creek Dam is also
rising still. Water levels on the Little Chena are still
gradually rising but it will be cresting soon as the rate of rise
has dropped off. Peak water levels near Moose Creek Dam will
likely be tonight through Saturday.

- This means low-lying and typical flood-prone areas may
experience areas of flooding through the end of the week as water
levels gradually rise then fall. In addition, other creeks and
streams in the vicinity will be running at elevated levels.

- For more updated river information, please refer to
water.noaa.gov or weather.gov/aprfc
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor the latest forecasts and be alert for possible
Flood Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be
prepared to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT THROUGH SATURDAY AFTERNOON

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 18 at 6:21AM CDT until September 19 at 7:00AM CDT by NWS Twin Cities/Chanhassen MN
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Freeborn County.

* WHEN...From this evening through Saturday morning.

* IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- There will be two rounds of rain today. A steady, light to
moderate rain today, then the potential for training
thunderstorms with heavy rainfall this evening. Where repeated
rounds of storms move across the same area, there will be a
threat for flash flooding, with maximum rainfall totals of 5 to 7
inches possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

Forecast effective for Shelby County Tennessee, Crittenden County
Arkansas, and DeSoto County Mississippi, including the city of
Memphis for today. This ozone forecast is due to forecasted ozone

people with respiratory disease, such as asthma, limit prolonged
outdoor exertion.

until monitored values return to safe levels. For more information go
to www.airnow.gov.

properties.description:
AQAFWD

The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ) has issued
an Ozone Action Day for the Dallas-Fort Worth area for Friday,
September 18, 2026.

Atmospheric conditions are expected to be favorable for producing
high levels of ozone air pollution in the Dallas-Fort Worth area
on Friday. You can help prevent ozone pollution by sharing a
ride, walking, riding a bicycle, taking your lunch to work,
avoiding drive-through lanes, conserving energy, and keeping your
vehicle properly tuned.

For more information on ozone:

Ozone: The Facts (www.tceq.texas.gov/goto/ozonefacts)

Air North Texas: (www.airnorthtexas.org)

EPA Air Now
(www.airnow.gov/index.cfm?action.local_state&STATEID=45&TAB=0)

Take care of Texas (www.takecareoftexas.org)

North Central Texas Council of Governments Air Quality
(www.nctcog.org/trans/air/index.asp)

properties.areaDesc: Madison; St. Clair; Monroe; St. Charles; Franklin; St. Louis; St. Louis City; Jefferson
properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued September 17 at 3:27PM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
The St. Louis Clean Air Partnership has issued an air quality alert
for the St. Louis metropolitan area from 10 AM to 8 PM CDT Friday.

An Orange air quality forecast means that maximum ozone
concentrations are expected to reach levels that pose a health risk.
Adverse health effects increase as air quality deteriorates. Ground-
level ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing
difficulties for children, older adults, as well as persons with
respiratory problems.

Reducing outdoor physical activity is recommended. If it is a
regularly scheduled work day you are urged to consider
telecommuting, carpooling, or utilizing public transit. Avoid
excessive idling and do not top off when refueling motor vehicles.
The use of gasoline-powered lawn equipment should be reduced or
postponed until late in the day.

For more information visit the St. Louis Clean Air Partnership at
http://cleanair-stlouis.com/

For current Air Quality Index (AQI) values visit
https://www.airnow.gov/

properties.areaDesc: Upper Chena River Valley; Two Rivers; Fairbanks Metro Area
properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued September 17 at 10:47AM AKDT until September 19 at 8:45AM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Chena River Basin from Moose Creek Dam to the end of Chena
Hot Springs Road.

* WHEN...Until 845 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Water over roadways. River or stream flows are elevated. Ponding of
water in areas is occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1042 AM AKDT, gauge reports indicated heavy rain across the
advisory area. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly, especially near Chena River. Between 1.5 and 2 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.25 inches
are possible in the advisory area.
- For Chena River below Hunts Creek near Two Rivers :
At 10:00am the stage was 14.9 feet.
Flood Stage is 17.2 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 16.2 feet is expected at 10:00am Friday.

- For Chena River below Moose Creek dam:
At 10:00am the stage was 22.1 feet.
Flood Stage is 24.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 25.0 feet is expected at 4:00am
Saturday.

- For Chena River near Two Rivers:
At 10:00am the stage was 19.4 feet.
Flood Stage is 19.5 feet.
Forecast: A crest around 20.1 feet is expected at 10:00pm
Thursday.


- Http://www.weather.gov/aprfc
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT UNTIL 845 AM AKDT SATURDAY

properties.description:
AQAFFC

The Georgia Department of Natural Resources, Environmental
Protection Division has issued a Code Orange (Unhealthy for
sensitive groups) Air Quality Alert for Atlanta for
Friday September 18.

Under Code Orange conditions, the outdoor air quality is likely to
be unhealthy for some people. Children, people who are sensitive to
ozone, and people with heart or lung disease should limit prolonged
outdoor exertion during the late afternoon or early evening when
ozone concentrations are highest.

For additional information on the Air Quality Index, please visit
http://airnow.gov.
